rca.rootCause: When writing a DS (Decimal String) data element with a value length exceeding 65534 bytes in Explicit VR transfer syntax, the writer attempts to encode the length using a 2-byte unsigned short (write_leUS), which overflows and raises a struct.error. The correct behavior per DICOM standard is to change the VR to UN (Unknown) when the value is too long for the explicit VR length field, as noted in issue #900. The current code does not handle this case and instead lets the low-level pack call fail with an unhelpful error message.
evidence: The issue describes an exception 'ushort format requires 0 <= number <= (0x7fff * 2 + 1)' raised by the pack call in write_leUS when writing a DS tag with length > 65534 bytes in explicit VR.
The hint states: 'Reopen as the fix is incorrect - the VR shall be changed to UN instead (see #900).'

The DICOM standard PS3.5 Table 6.2-1 note says: 'Data Elements with multiple values using this VR may not be properly encoded if Explicit-VR transfer syntax is used and the VL of this attribute exceeds 65534 bytes.'
The repo map shows pydicom/filewriter.py as the file containing write_data_element and write_leUS functions.
